newsitem.title: UK: UK charity funds beat indices in 1996 -- survey.
newsitem.headline: UK charity funds beat indices in 1996 -- survey.

text.p: UK charity funds outperformed the main indices in almost all sectors in 1996, a report on the sector from the WM Company said.

The report, surveying more than 350 charity funds with total assets of 10 billion stg, said funds produced an average overall return of 11.7 percent in 1996, above the three year return of eight percent and close to the 12.1 percent average return of the past 10 years.
It said UK equities were the best performing major sector, earning some 17.1 percent against a FTSE All-Share return of 16.7 percent.
In overseas investments, charity funds outperformed or matched the key indices in all but one of the major markets -- the Pacific excluding Japan.
Overall overseas returns of 2.6 percent were ahead of the FT/S&P World (ex UK) index return of 1.4 percent.
"North America and Europe both delivered strong returns of over 12 percent, but the negative return from Japan of minus 22 percent was disappointing," WM director Peter Warrington said.
"The benefits of overseas investments generally were reduced by the strong appreciation of sterling during the year."

WM said performance was not significantly affected by the differing investment objectives of the funds, although those funds with a requirement to provide a high level of income slightly outperformed those with full discretion and those with asset mix restrictions.
Funds with high income targets have a relatively high proportion of their assets in UK bonds.

"While this may have held them back, its effect was offset by their light exposure to those overseas markets which performed poorly and they suffered less from sterling's appreciation," Warrington said.
